implementation_notes: Blazor's composition model gives the family both halves: the parent receives its children as a RenderFragment (so the call site decides which parts exist and in what order) and publishes its state to any descendant with <CascadingValue Value=this>, which children read through a [CascadingParameter] property - the parent's method is then called directly by the child, so no call-site wiring exists. Mark a value IsFixed when it never changes to skip the re-render subscriptions cascading values otherwise create. The classic structure only has to be written by hand when the invariant cannot live in a component (for example state that must survive navigation), and then a plain parent-owned service takes over.
pitfalls: An unmatched [CascadingParameter] compiles and renders with null - a child then silently does nothing; throw in OnParametersSet when the parent is absent.
Every child that consumes a non-fixed cascading value re-renders whenever the parent re-renders; cascading a large object graph is a common performance trap.
Cascading by type succeeds silently when two nested parents provide the same type - name the value and read it with Name to avoid attaching to the wrong ancestor.

variants.name: WPF logical tree: attached properties and inherited DataContext
variants.implementation_notes: In WPF the parent-child channel is the logical tree: an attached property lets a child report a value on a property registered by the parent type (Microsoft's own phrasing: "An attached property lets a child element specify a unique value for a property that's defined in a parent element"), which the parent reads during measure/arrange - Grid.Row and Canvas.Left are the canonical members of such a family. State flows the other way through the inherited DataContext, so children binding to the parent's properties share it implicitly, and an ItemsControl-generated family gets each child's data without call-site wiring. Choose this variant only in a WPF/XAML codebase: the classic pattern's re-render and lifetime machinery is the framework's, and hand-rolled parent walkers duplicate it badly.
variants.idiom_name: attached properties read by the parent plus the logical tree's inherited DataContext
pitfalls: Attached-property values are read at layout time: changing them without AffectsMeasure/AffectsRender metadata leaves the parent showing stale layout.
Inherited DataContext flows one object to every descendant; a child that wraps it in its own view model silently breaks the family's data contract.
Logical-tree membership is not visual containment - a popup or virtualized item can sit outside the parent element while still using its attached properties.
